client_profile.objective: Compare bonds, real estate, and S&P 500 exposure
client_profile.risk_tolerance: Show risk-averse, average, and risk-seeking alternatives
client_profile.liquidity_needs: Not specified; assess the selected vehicle before investing
constraints: Bond issuer and maturity mix not specified
Real-estate vehicle (direct property, listed REIT, or fund) not specified

assumptions_note: The return assumptions below are fictional demo inputs, not forecasts or current market estimates. Replace them with dated, reviewed research before using the results.

investment_options.name: Bond exposure
investment_options.instrument: Government/corporate mix, issuer quality, maturity, and currency unspecified
rewards: Coupon income can provide a more predictable cash-flow component than equities
High-quality bonds may diversify equity exposure
Bond prices may rise when market yields fall, depending on duration
risks: Issuer default or credit-spread widening can reduce value
Rising yields can lower the market value of existing fixed-rate bonds
Inflation can erode the purchasing power of fixed coupon and principal payments
Liquidity, reinvestment, and currency risks depend on the bond and vehicle

investment_options.name: Real-estate exposure
investment_options.instrument: Property fund/REIT or direct property not specified
rewards: Property can generate rental income and may appreciate in value
A diversified property vehicle can add an asset source distinct from public equities and bonds
Some listed REITs can be traded more readily than directly held property
risks: Direct property and non-traded vehicles can be illiquid, costly, and difficult to value
Property values and financing costs can be sensitive to interest rates
Vacancy, tenant default, maintenance, leverage, and geographic concentration can reduce returns
Listed REIT prices can fall with equity markets even when underlying property values change more slowly

sources.label: Investor.gov REIT benefits, risks, and liquidity distinctions

investment_options.name: S&P 500 exposure
investment_options.instrument: Index-tracker exposure; GBP hedging choice not specified
rewards: Exposure to large U.S. companies across multiple industries
Equity ownership offers potential long-term capital growth and dividend income
An index tracker can spread company-specific risk across its constituents
risks: Equity prices can fall sharply and losses are not capped at the supplied downside scenario
Market-cap weighting means the largest constituents can have an outsized effect on results
A GBP investor may gain or lose from USD/GBP exchange-rate movements if unhedged
The index is concentrated in U.S. equities and does not represent a globally diversified portfolio
